title: What the Monks of the Thebaid Reported
english: By the same, to the bishops in Libya and the Pentapolis.

We must take care over everything that is useful and needful for building up the people, and that also contributes to the good name of the holy churches. For it is written, “Make the children of Israel careful” (Leviticus 15:31). Now fathers of monasteries in the province of the Thebaid, devout men whose way of life deserves admiration, came to Alexandria; and when I asked them about the state of the monasteries there, they told me that many are taking offence, for the following reason.
1. That no one should be ordained without examination
Some men who have only just married, and who have come down, as it were, straight from the bridal chamber, sweep along some of the most God-loving…
translator_notes: Copy-text: the Greek text printed in PG 77.
The sign ∆ after the title is a collection/edition numeral and is not rendered; the page marker 282 is omitted.
Headings (Preface, 1.) render the bracketed and lettered headings of the edition, which are likely editorial or collection headings rather than Cyril's own words.

Leviticus 15:31: Cyril's εὐλαβεῖς ποιεῖτε τοὺς υἱοὺς Ἰσραήλ follows the Greek Old Testament (καὶ εὐλαβεῖς ποιήσετε τοὺς υἱοὺς Ισραηλ); the Hebrew reads 'keep the people of Israel separate from their uncleanness', so the English follows Cyril's Greek ('careful').
οὐκ ἀθαύμαστον ἔχοντες πολιτείαν: a litotes, 'having a not unadmirable way of life'; rendered 'whose way of life deserves admiration'.
σκανδαλίζονται: rendered 'are taking offence' (they are being made to stumble by what they see).

συναρπάζουσί: 'seize and carry along, hurry along'; the men press the bishops into hasty ordination. Rendered 'sweep along'. The sentence breaks at the section boundary and continues in the next section with 'bishops'; the closing ellipsis marks the break.
baehrens: PG 77; Ad episcopos Libyae et Pentapoleos ep open
